report.source_text: Histological analysis of both tonsils showed a lypmhoepithelial proliferation without any anomalies or signs of malignancy. The macroscopic appearance of the supraclavicular mass consisted of an elastic nodule, measured 3×1, 8×1 cm with a shiny myxoid cut surface (figure 2A). The whole-mount slide of the nodule showed a well-circumscribed intranodal lesion consisting of variable sized cystic structure intermixed with basophilic epithelial sheet and acidophilic stromal component (figure 2B). The microscopic analysis revealed an intranodal proliferation with a biphasic growth pattern of epithelial/myoepithelial cells and chondromyxoid stroma. Compact sheet of epithelial cells focally forming ductal structure were associated with less cohesive ovoid myoepithelial cells interspersed in a chondomyxoid stroma (figure 2C). A more oncocyte type of epithelium layered some of the ductal structure (figure 2D), the mitotic index MIB was at 14%. In immunostaining study, this proliferation was positive for the following markers: SOX10, P63, GFAP and keratin 5/6 with partial expression for Gata 3 and cytokeratin 7. There was no expression for CEA, Actin, PAX8, chromogranin, synaptophysin, CK20, PSA, HMB45, TTF1 and CDX2.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 72-year-old male with a history of melanoma presented with a progressive left-sided supraclavicular mass. Initial fine needle aspiration biopsy was inconclusive, showing atypical epithelial cells but no melanoma. Subsequent detailed histopathological and immunohistochemical analysis of the excised mass revealed an intranodal lesion with biphasic epithelial/myoepithelial cells and chondromyxoid stroma, consistent with benign salivary tissue proliferation type pleomorphic adenoma within a lymph node. Post-surgical follow-up with cervical ultrasonography at 3 months showed no recurrence of the tumor.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with a left-sided supraclavicular mass, progressive over 4 months, with a history of melanoma.

Initial FNA showed atypical epithelial cells but no melanoma cells, with cohesive sheets of cells, increased nucleocytoplasmic ratio, intermixed plasmocytoid discohesive cells, and rare oncocyte cells.

Histopathological analysis of the excised mass revealed an intranodal lesion, 3x1.8x1 cm, with a biphasic growth pattern of epithelial/myoepithelial cells and chondromyxoid stroma, including ductal structures and oncocyte-type epithelium.

Immunostaining showed positivity for SOX10, P63, GFAP, keratin 5/6, partial Gata 3 and cytokeratin 7, and negativity for CEA, Actin, PAX8, chromogranin, synaptophysin, CK20, PSA, HMB45, TTF1, and CDX2.
Microscopic and immunostaining findings were compatible with benign salivary tissue proliferation type pleomorphic adenoma into a lymph node.
Cervical ultrasonography 3 months post-surgery showed no recurrence of the tumor.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial FNA showed no melanoma cells; immunohistochemistry was negative for HMB45 and other melanoma markers, and positive for epithelial/myoepithelial markers, ruling out melanoma.

Immunohistochemistry was negative for various markers associated with other malignancies (e.g., CEA, CK20, TTF1, CDX2), and the overall histopathological pattern was consistent with a benign pleomorphic adenoma.

remaining_uncertainties: Detailed findings from initial imaging studies (e.g., ultrasound, CT, MRI) of the supraclavicular mass were not documented.
